project.objective: Where was Elena Asmundsdotter — the mother of Asmund Jönsson (born 11 September 1718 in Barsebäck parish, Malmöhus, Sweden) — born, and who were her parents?

questions.question: In which parish was Elena Asmundsdotter — wife of Jöns Jönsson and mother of Asmund Jönsson (baptized 11 September 1718 in Barsebäck parish, Malmöhus, Sweden) — born?
questions.rationale: Establishing Elena's birth parish is the gatekeeper step for the entire objective. Swedish husförhörslängd (household examination records) for Barsebäck parish routinely record each parishioner's home parish of origin; once that parish is identified, its birth/baptism register can be searched for Elena's baptism entry, which will name her parents and confirm the birth location. Without the birth parish, the parentage question cannot be efficiently pursued. Barsebäck is in Malmöhus County (Skåne); records from the late 17th–early 18th century are available on FamilySearch and SVAR/Riksarkivet.

exhaustive_declaration.justification: Two accessible, unsearched records prevent declaration. (1) The Barsebäck husförhörslängd (household examination register) in volume 004514823 is the single most direct source for a birth-parish identification in Swedish genealogy — it would record Elena's origin parish beside her household entry. pli_003 browsed only 4 of 749 images and explicitly did not reach the household examination section; this is a resource-limit gap, not inaccessibility. (2) Volume 004516862 (Kavlinge/Höj kyrkobok 1662-1729, pli_008) was skipped as 'church financial accounts,' but the rationale does not document which images were examined to confirm this. If the volume contains baptism entries for pre-1685 Källinge, it would hold Elena's actual baptism record — the most direct answer to the birth-parish and parentage questions. These two records must be browsed before the accumulated convergent evidence from Källinge (src_001 through src_004) can be considered exhaustively tested. ArkivDigital (pli_005) is inaccessible in autonomous mode and does not constitute a blocking gap because it covers the same physical records already partially accessed via FamilySearch.

stop_criteria.goal_alignment: Partially met. Four independent source lines (LDS compiled genealogy, Källinge 1693 godmother appearance, 1698-1699 godmother/marriage cluster, 1700-1701 Asmund-family cluster) converge on Källinge (Keflinge) parish as Elena's home parish, and Jöns Jönsson appears with a daughter in Källinge 1703. No competing evidence names any other parish. However, no source directly states Elena was born in Källinge; all evidence is residential presence and family-cluster inference. The husförhörslängd would provide the explicit institutional statement of origin the GPS standard requires.
stop_criteria.repository_breadth: Not yet met. FamilySearch indexed aggregates (national), FamilySearch full-text corpus, and the Källinge kyrkobok 1685-1733 were adequately searched. The Barsebäck husförhörslängd section (volume 004514823, 749 images) was not navigated — only 4 images were browsed and the household examination section was not reached. Volume 004516862 (Kavlinge 1662-1729) was skipped without documented image verification of its content type. ArkivDigital is inaccessible in autonomous mode (external paid site).
stop_criteria.original_substitution: Partially met. The Källinge sources (src_002, src_003, src_004) are 1758 copies by Pastor P. Stevenius — derivatives one level from the original registers. The LDS genealogy (src_001) is a 20th-century compiled derivative. No original 17th-century register was accessed directly. Volume 004516862 may contain the original pre-1685 Källinge baptism entries that would be the true original source.
stop_criteria.independent_verification: Partially met. Two genuinely independent informant lines corroborate Källinge: (a) the 1954 LDS compiler (src_001) working from unspecified underlying records, and (b) the 1758 Stevenius copies of the Källinge kyrkobok (src_002/003/004). The Stevenius copies all share a single copyist and count as one informant unit. Neither source directly states Elena's birth in Källinge — both establish family presence and association. Two independent units is minimally sufficient, but the evidence is indirect rather than primary-information birth-record confirmation.
stop_criteria.evidence_class: Partially met. src_003 and src_004 are primary information (parish clerk at official duty) for the events they record in Källinge — the stillbirth entry, marriage entry, godmother appearances. These are original-record quality for what they directly record. However, none of the sources is a birth or baptism record for Elena herself, nor a husförhörslängd entry explicitly noting her origin parish. The evidence class is primary for the family-cluster facts but indirect for the birth-parish conclusion.
stop_criteria.conflict_resolution: Met. No registered conflicts. The internal tension between the LDS archive's 'Asmund Hansson' label and the log_011 finding that Åsmund Hansson first married as a bachelor in 1704 was resolved during research: the younger Åsmund Hansson (married 1704) is distinct from the older Asmund who died c.1699 and whose sons (Anders, Nielz, Gunne, Måns Asmundson) are documented in Källinge 1700-1701.
stop_criteria.overturn_risk: Elevated until the Barsebäck husförhörslängd is searched. The husförhörslängd is the institutional record created for the specific purpose of recording each parishioner's origin parish. If Elena's entry records a parish other than Källinge, the conclusion changes. This is not a hypothetical risk — it is the exact information the record captures. The accumulated convergent evidence makes Källinge the overwhelming probability, but the accessible unsearched record means the overturn risk cannot honestly be called low.

items.rationale: Search the indexed FamilySearch aggregate collections — 'Sweden, Baptisms, 1611-1920' (collection 1520594, 7M+ records) and 'Sweden, Marriages, 1630-1920' (collection 1520596) — for entries naming Elena Asmundsdotter or Helena Asmundsdotter in Barsebäck or Harjager härad, Malmöhus. The Malmöhus county-level collection (1974200) shows 0 indexed records, so coverage is uncertain, but the national aggregate extracts may include partial Malmöhus entries. A name-indexed hit here is the fastest possible resolution. Search both 'Elena' and 'Helena' (Swedish variants) with 'Asmundsdotter' as surname. If the marriage register entry for Jöns Jönsson and Elena is among the indexed records, it may name her father (Asmund) and origin parish directly.

Full-text co-occurrence search for 'Asmund' and 'Helena' (or 'Elena') as separate required terms across the Swedish FamilySearch corpus, executed via the search-full-text skill, unscoped. Even though the identified Barsebäck volumes (004514823_001/002/003) are not full-text searchable, other Malmöhus-adjacent volumes in the corpus may be AI-transcribed and searchable. This approach can surface records not name-indexed: the husförhörslängd entry recording Elena's origin, her baptism in a neighboring parish naming her father Asmund, or a marriage entry citing both names. Elena's patronym 'Asmundsdotter' identifies her father's first name as Asmund (also spelled Åsmund or Esmund) — a relatively uncommon name in 18th-century Skåne — making this co-occurrence distinctive. Per the record-type guide, this tactic is recommended for unindexed parish registers.

Browse the three main Barsebäck church-record image groups on FamilySearch (004514823_001: 157 images; 004514823_002: 428 images; 004514823_003: 164 images; total 749 images) covering 1648-1861. All are 0% name-indexed and not full-text searchable — they must be read page by page in Swedish (18th-century Gothic script). The husförhörslängd (household examination register) is the highest-priority section: these periodic registers list every parishioner in the household with their origin parish noted (typically as 'f. i [parish]' = born in [parish]). Locate Jöns Jönsson's household; Elena's entry should record her birth parish. Also examine the inflyttningslängd (in-migration register) for an entry showing Elena arriving from another parish, and the vigselbok (marriage register) for the Jöns Jönsson–Elena Asmundsdotter marriage, which may name her father or origin. The loc_001 locality entry identifies the 428-image vol. 004514823_002 as the largest and most likely to contain the continuous household register — start there.

items.jurisdiction: Barsebäck, Harjager, Malmöhus, Sweden; Hofterup, Harjager, Malmöhus, Sweden
items.rationale: Browse the three combined Barsebäck+Hofterup image groups on FamilySearch (004514824_001: 258 images; 004514824_002: 257 images; 004514824_003: 28 images; total 543 images) covering 1696-1729. Locality guide (loc_001) confirms these volumes serve both Barsebäck and the neighboring Hofterup parish jointly — all pages must be browsed. Since Asmund Jönsson was baptized 11 September 1718, the marriage of his parents Jöns Jönsson and Elena Asmundsdotter likely falls between ca. 1710-1718, squarely within this date window. The vigselbok (marriage register) in this volume is the most targeted source: marriage entries in Skåne Lutheran parishes of this era often note the bride's father and home parish. Also examine any husförhörslängd pages for Elena's household entry with origin notation. Record 0% indexed, browse-only, in Swedish.

Search ArkivDigital (arkivdigital.se, subscription) for Barsebäck parish records. ArkivDigital holds high-resolution scans of Swedish church records, including Malmöhus county, and is often preferred over FamilySearch for Skåne parishes because image quality is superior. If FamilySearch image groups 004514823 or 004514824 prove illegible due to scan quality or ink degradation, ArkivDigital's scans of the same original registers may be readable. ArkivDigital also provides an online transcription community (Svenska kyrkoarkiv) whose transcriptions may index names not found in FamilySearch's collections. Fallback for item 3 (FamilySearch browse of 004514823 volumes).

Search the Riksarkivet mantalslängder (poll-tax/household-tax registers, available at sok.riksarkivet.se/mantalslangder, 1642-1820) for Barsebäck parish. These annual household-tax records enumerate heads of household and family members, with women listed under their husbands. While mantalslängder rarely record birth parish, they can: (a) confirm Elena's presence in Jöns Jönsson's Barsebäck household in the years before and after 1718; (b) reveal whether a man named Asmund appears in Barsebäck or neighboring parishes (Elena's father may have been a local figure); (c) provide context for the household composition. Supplements the husförhörslängd and fills in years where the husförhörslängd is missing or illegible.

FAN search: browse church records of neighboring Harjager härad parishes (Hofterup, Vallkärra, Landskrona, and other parishes bordering Barsebäck) for a man named Asmund or Åsmund who could be Elena's father. Elena's patronym 'Asmundsdotter' reveals her father's first name was Asmund — a relatively uncommon first name in 18th-century Skåne. If Asmund appears in a neighboring parish's records (as a householder, baptism father, or marriage party), that parish is Elena's likely birth parish. This search targets records of an associate (Elena's father) that directly bear on the subject of q_001 (Elena's birth parish). FamilySearch collection 1974200 (Sweden, Malmöhus, Church Records, 1541-1918) holds browse-only images for the relevant parishes. Searching for 'Asmund' in adjacent parishes serves as both a FAN lead and a narrowing tool for where to search Elena's baptism.

Primary target for q_001: the Kavlinge+Höj church register 004516862 (1662-1729) is the only FamilySearch volume covering the period when Elena Asmundsdotter was likely baptized (~1685-1700). The LDS genealogy archive (src_001) identifies her as 'Elina Asmundsson' daughter of Asmund Hansson, associated with Kavlinge/Harjager härad. Browse the dopbok section for entries naming father Asmund and daughter Elina/Elena/Helena. Also check husförhörslängd for Asmund Hansson's household. Supersedes pli_003 in priority because it targets the identified birth parish.

Secondary Kavlinge search: 004516861 series covers Kavlinge+Höj 1685-1733 with overlap with 004516862. Browse for baptisms, marriages (find Asmund Hansson + wife Hanna marriage record for mother's maiden name), and husförhörslängd showing the Asmund Hansson family. The parents' marriage record names the mother's maiden surname, essential for full parentage.

log.notes: 622 Sweden-wide results returned; top-ranked matches are from Halland, Älvsborg, and Göteborg och Bohus — none from Malmöhus county. Consistent with locality guide finding that collection 1974200 (Malmöhus Church Records) has 0 indexed records. No match for Elena Asmundsdotter of Barsebäck.
617 Sweden-wide results for 'Helena' variant; same pattern — top candidates from Halland, Älvsborg, Göteborg och Bohus, none from Malmöhus. No match for the Barsebäck subject.

Only 5 results for Elena Asmundsdotter + spouse Jöns in Swedish marriage records; all 5 have spouses named Jonas (not Jöns Jönsson) or are from wrong counties. No marriage record for Elena Asmundsdotter and Jöns Jönsson in indexed collections.

Same result as Elena variant — 5 results, none matching Jöns Jönsson + Malmöhus. Indexed search for pli_001 exhausted. Answer is in unindexed browse-only Barsebäck images (pli_003, pli_004) or ArkivDigital (pli_005).

FTS co-occurrence search for father-name Asmund + given name Helena across full FamilySearch corpus (no collection scope, no place filter). 69 total results, 20 examined. All results are from US records (Delaware Swedish colonial settlements, Utah genealogy archives, North Dakota and Montana cemeteries). No results from Malmöhus Sweden church records — Barsebäck volumes (004514823, 004514824 series) are browse-only with fulltextSearchable: false, confirming they are not in the FTS corpus. One derivative Utah genealogy archive result (1948, place 'Malmohus') mentions Helena and Hanna Asmundsson with dates 1667–1718 but is a compiled secondary source; may reflect the correct family but cannot substitute for original records. Negative for original Swedish parish evidence.

FTS co-occurrence search variant with Elena spelling (vs Helena). 10 total results, all examined. Results are Norwegian immigration records, Guatemala baptism records, and US birth/marriage records — entirely unrelated. No Swedish Malmöhus parish content. Confirms that the Barsebäck/Malmöhus volumes are absent from the FTS-indexed corpus regardless of given-name spelling. Negative.

FTS search for distinctive patronym +Asmundsdotter across full corpus (no scope). 5 results: 2x North Dakota Icelandic-American cemetery (1990), 1 Quebec passenger list 1879 (Icelandic immigrant Thorda Asmundsdotter), 1 Goteborg Sweden probate (Anna Asmundsdotter, different county), 1 Michigan biography 1986 (Anne Asmundsdotter, Norwegian immigrant). None from Malmöhus or Barsebäck. Confirmed FTS corpus does not include Malmöhus browse-only volumes. Negative.

FTS co-occurrence +Asmund +Malmohus across full corpus (no scope). 56 total results, 20 examined. All results are from LDS/Utah genealogy archive collection M9J1-LMH (Salt Lake City 1940s-1950s compiled genealogies of Swedish Malmöhus families). Critical leads identified: (1) ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L9QY-4758 - 'ASMUND HANSSON' from Kavlinge, Malmöhus with daughter 'Elina Asmundsson' and dates 1675-1736 -- Elina/Elena Asmundsdotter daughter of Asmund Hansson is a strong candidate for the subject; (2) ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G979-73HC and ark:/61903/3:1:3QSQ-G979-7397 - both name 'ASMUND JONSSON' with explicit place 'Barseback' and 'Malmohus'; (3) multiple other compiled genealogies name men called Asmund in Malmöhus parishes near Barsebäck (Kavlinge, Genarp, Skurup, V. Sallerup, V. Karaby). These are derived/compiled sources (non-original); originals would be Swedish church registers. Priority for record-extraction: ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L9QY-4758 (Asmund Hansson + daughter Elina Asmundsson, Kavlinge).

log.notes: Browsed images 257-310 of sub-volume _004 (151 images total): images 257-298 cover Höj parish births 1685-1730; images 299-310 cover Källinge parish births 1685-1705. Key findings: (1) Image 301 (Källinge 1686-1687): Asmund Larsson married Gertrud Nilsdotter January 1686 — candidate father for Elena Asmundsdotter. (2) Image 302 (1688-1689): No daughter of Asmund named Elina/Elena in 1688 or 1689; 1689 entry is 'Johne Asmundssons lilla Son'. (3) Image 303 (1690-1691): No Asmund daughter named Elena. (4) Image 310 (1704-1705): Åsmund Hansson married first time as bachelor ('Ungkarl') September 1704 to Kirsti Peder Bengts dotter — eliminates him as father of an Elena born pre-1704. Multiple adult women identified as daughters of an Asmund active in Källinge c.1704-1705 (Ingar, Sophia/Soshia, Luse/Lucia). Källinge births for ~1692-1703 (images ~304-309) not yet browsed. Target birth entry (Elena/Elina daughter of Asmund Larsson, ~1687-1700) not yet located.

Continuation browse of Källinge section, images 304-309 (years 1692-1703). Key findings: (1) Image 304 (1692-1693): 'Elina Asmundz dotter tog af håfwedet' at baptism of Oluf Larsson's son Hans, October 1693 — CONFIRMS Elena Asmundsdotter as adult woman in Källinge in 1693; she was born before ~1680 (too early for the 1685-1733 register). (2) Image 308 (1700-1701): 'Gumma Asmunds Enckia' (widow of Asmund) had a stillborn February 1700 — confirms older Asmund died ~1699 in Källinge. Sons: Anders Asmundson (godfather 1700), Nielz Asmundson (married 1701), Gunne Asmundson (godfather 1701). Also 'Asmund Kåhlson' married Marna Nils Jöns in early 1700 (different Asmund). (3) Image 309 (1702-1703): 'Jöns Jönssons lilla dotter' Kirstina born 28 September 1703 in Källinge — Elena's husband Jöns Jönsson likely had a child in Källinge before the family moved to Barsebäck (where Asmund Jönsson was born 1718). Elena's baptism predates this register (born before 1685). Her father = the older Asmund who died ~1699 in Källinge; his full name not recoverable from this register. LDS archive's 'Asmund Hansson' patronymic is contradicted — Åsmund Hansson first married as bachelor 1704, precluding fatherhood of Elena.

The primary purpose of this item was to confirm Elena's presence in Jöns Jönsson's Barsebäck household, which is established by the original research objective (Asmund Jönsson was baptized in Barsebäck 1718 with parents named). Tax records would not advance q_001 (birth parish of Elena). Autonomous mode: external site access (Riksarkivet) not available.

Källinge kyrkobok 1698-1699 (image 307). Key findings: (1) 1698 entry 1: 'Anders Asmundssons dotter' (daughter of Anders Asmundson, himself a son of the older Asmund) baptized January 1698. (2) 1698 entry 2: 'Jöns Olofssons lilla dotter... Asmunds dotter bar barnet' — 'Asmunds dotter' (daughter of Asmund) carried Jöns Olofsson's newborn daughter Elina at her baptism (July 1698) — another godparent appearance of Elena/Asmundsdotter in Källinge. (3) 1698 marriage 1: 'Per Nilson af Foullatompta och Margreta Asmunds dotter blefwo trolofwade och efter 3nde lysning sammanwiggde Dom: Invocavit' — SISTER of Elena: Margreta Asmundsdotter married Per Nilsson of Foullatompta in Källinge 1698. (4) 1699 entry 7: 'Asmunds dotter fick bet öfwer dopet' — another godmother appearance of Elena/Asmundsdotter in Källinge (December 1699). No marriage of Jöns Jönsson and Elena Asmundsdotter found in 1698-1699 Källinge register. Confirming: the Asmund family cluster in Källinge is now established 1693-1705 across images 304, 307, 308, 310.

Attempted navigation of Barsebäck church records (004514823, 749 images). Image 1: blank folio '144964'. Image 50: Danish-era baptism entries from c.1640s-1650s. Image 220: folio 112-113, Danish-Swedish mixed language, c.1685 era, 'Gifte' (marriage) column empty for this spread. Image 300: folio 270-271, baptisms for 1730-1731, no marriages. Could not navigate to the husförhörslängd section (likely in later sub-volume _002 or _003) or to the 1700-1715 marriage section. Volume structure requires systematic browse from image ~190-260 to reach the 1700-1715 period but browse budget exhausted for this session. The marriage of Jöns Jönsson and Elena Asmundsdotter was not found in Barsebäck records.

Volume 004514824 found to be IN-MIGRATION ATTESTATION CERTIFICATES (Inflyttnings-Attester) for 1825-1830, not the 1696-1729 marriage/baptism register the plan assumed. This is a different record type than intended. The 1696-1729 Barsebäck+Hofterup church records (birth/marriage/death) are not in this volume. Marked as skipped — wrong record type, not applicable to q_001.

Her role 'tog af håfwedet' (took off the christening cap) is the godparent function of removing the cap at baptism, an honor typically given to a local resident. The patronymic 'Asmundzdotter' is rare, matching the patronymic of the tree subject Elena Asmundsdotter (wife of Jöns Jönsson, mother of Asmund Jönsson baptized Barsebäck 11 Sept. 1718). quirks: All Barsebäck parish records on FamilySearch are browse-only images (0% name-indexed, not full-text searchable) — they must be browsed page-by-page in Swedish.
FamilySearch volumes 004514824_001/002/003 cover Barsebäck AND Hofterup jointly for 1696-1729; browse all pages in those volumes.

Husförhörslängd (household examination registers) are the highest-priority source for finding a parishioner's origin parish — locate Elena's household entry in Barsebäck to find her birth parish notation.

Elena's patronym 'Asmundsdotter' reveals her father's first name was Asmund (or Åsmund/Esmund) — once her origin parish is identified, search its dopbok for a child named Elena/Helena with father Asmund.
Inflyttningslängd (in-migration registers) in Barsebäck will record Elena's origin parish if she moved there from elsewhere.

Skåne was Danish territory until the Treaty of Roskilde (1658); records before that date are Danish. Swedish church record-keeping was established quickly after 1658; all records for 1680-1750 are in Swedish.
Husförhörslängd in Skåne parishes typically begin ca. 1686; earlier years may lack household examination records.
ArkivDigital (arkivdigital.se, subscription) often has clearer, higher-resolution scans of Malmöhus records than FamilySearch — preferred when FamilySearch images are illegible.
Mantalslängder (poll-tax registers) 1642-1820 are searchable at Riksarkivet (sok.riksarkivet.se/mantalslangder) and supplement husförhörslängd for household enumeration.

FamilySearch wiki pages were unavailable during this survey (server offline) — consult https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Sweden_Genealogy and https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Malmöhus_Genealogy directly for additional guidance.
